conventions.convention: Success requires a containing finite dyadic interval or rectangle whose radius is at most the absolute tolerance. Complex radius is half the Euclidean diagonal. Relative certification additionally requires zero exclusion and rad(B)/d(B,0) ≤ the relative tolerance; absolute success need not pass the relative test.
The Gauss function denotes only its power-series branch for |z|<1, with c not a nonpositive integer.

The continued log-Gamma branch is defined on C minus the nonpositive real axis by right-half-plane evaluation and subtraction of principal logarithms of shift factors; it is not principal Log(Gamma(z)).
Spherical functions use positive real arguments and the outgoing exp(iz) convention, with h₀⁽¹⁾(z)=-i exp(iz)/z.

DJsc and DHsc are scaled argument derivatives of the original spherical functions, not derivatives of the scaled functions. Point inputs require terminating dyadic enclosure interfaces; fixed interval inputs request whole images and have no arbitrary-precision success promise.
The integer modified-Bessel output is exp(-x)I_n(x) for x≥0. The auxiliary D sequence starts with D₀=-J₁ and D₁=J₀ and is not the Bessel function of the second kind.
Airy coefficients satisfy c₂=0 and c_{k+3}=c_k/((k+3)(k+2)); Bi(0)=1/(3^(1/6)Gamma(2/3)).

erfcx and its moment/continued-fraction branches here require x>0. The asymptotic remainder and finite-depth continued fraction are finite certificates, without convergence assertions as truncation or depth increases.

load_bearing.statement: A success enclosure contains the exact requested value and has radius at most εa. Relative certification requires zero exclusion and rad(B)/d(B,0)≤εr. Finite caps do not imply success for every input.

Every success output encloses each requested scaled or unscaled value, or the entire requested image for an interval input, and satisfies its absolute-radius test. Every capped execution terminates. For each fixed order, positive represented real point, finite nonempty target list, and positive rational absolute tolerances, some finite work, degree, interface-index, and precision caps permit absolute success.

On z>0, jℓ and hℓ⁽¹⁾ solve the degree-ℓ radial Helmholtz equation, satisfy the stated order and derivative recurrences, have the stated regular-origin and outgoing-infinity normalizations, and satisfy jℓ(hℓ⁽¹⁾)′−jℓ′hℓ⁽¹⁾=i/z².

For any finite dyadic rectangle Z contained in the slit plane, whenever the Gamma/log-Gamma algorithm returns success, its enclosure contains the requested function range on Z and passes the absolute-radius test. Every execution with finite caps terminates; universal success is not asserted.
For Re z>0, the series defining ℓ₊ converges locally uniformly, defines a holomorphic function, and satisfies exp(ℓ₊(z))=Gamma(z).
For x>0 the moments are finite and positive, satisfy 2xM₀+2M₁=1 and kM_{k−1}=2xM_k+2M_{k+1}; their ratios satisfy r_k=(k+1)/(2(x+r_{k+1})), 0<r_k<(k+1)/(2x), and erfcx(x)=1/(sqrt(pi)(x+r₀)).

For n≥0 the J_n and I_n series converge absolutely and locally uniformly, as do their first two formal derivative series. If K≥0 and q=|z|²/[4(K+2)(K+n+2)]<1, the tail after indices 0 through K is bounded by |a_{K+1}|/(1−q), with the stated zero-argument cases.

For x>0, N≥1, 0≤n<N, q=−J_{N+1}/D_{N+1} with D_{N+1}≠0, and s∈{0,1} with J_s+qD_s≠0, the normalized backward value satisfies Jhat_n−J_n=q(J_sD_n−J_nD_s)/(J_s+qD_s). No convergence as N tends to infinity is asserted.

alerts.finding: In lem-pe18-outgoing-spherical-mode-expansion, F3 cites the spherical supplier and says hℓ⁽¹⁾ "obeys $h_\ell'=h_{\ell-1}-(\ell+1)h_\ell/z$" without restricting ℓ. The supplier lem-spherical-bessel-and-hankel-radial-solutions states this identity only for ℓ≥1. The consumer includes ℓ=0, where its displayed h_{−1} is undefined under the cited definitions. Its radiation calculation at ℓ=0 can instead use direct differentiation of h₀⁽¹⁾=-i exp(iz)/z.

seams_checked.note: The Boys algorithm and soundness theorem use Gamma only on positive half-integer singleton rectangles, project successful rectangles onto the real coordinate, retain child work accounting, and do not infer universal success. Their absolute and relative tests preserve the common result contract. No reverse dependency was found.

The radial theorem uses the positive-real spherical equation, outgoing normalization, and Wronskian faithfully. Its numerical interface distinguishes argument derivatives from radial derivatives and constructs a terminating interface for kR. The square-well example also constructs sqrt(k²+V₀)R and retains a nonzero matching denominator. No reverse dependency was found.

The outgoing sign and positive-flux Wronskian use in lem-pe18-spherical-hankel-radial-identities are faithful. F3 of lem-pe18-outgoing-spherical-mode-expansion omits the supplier's ℓ≥1 restriction on its derivative recurrence; this is recorded in alerts. The ℓ=0 case needs the base formula. No reverse dependency was found.
